pageCache.text:
Welcome
At John Hampden Primary School, we are proud to live by The Hampden Way:
We are a team. We do our best. We are kind.
These simple yet powerful values shape everything we do. They guide our learning, our relationships, and our commitment to helping every child thrive.
The Hampden Way

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care - John Hampden Primary School
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care
At John Hampden School, we are committed to supporting the whole child — academically, socially and emotionally. Our pastoral care team works closely with pupils and families to ensure every child feels safe, valued and ready to learn. Through nurturing relationships, early support and a range of tailored interventions, we aim to help every child thrive.
Explore the links below to find out more about the support available:

pageCache.pageTitle: ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support Assistant) - John Hampden Primary School
pageCache.text:
ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support Assistant)
At John Hampden School we believe that to enable our pupils to learn effectively, they need to feel safe in their environment and be both socially and emotionally ready to learn. We understand the importance of holistic development and offer nurturing and enriching experiences to enable the development of the whole child. We recognise that some of our pupils are not always emotionally ready to learn. Class teachers will refer pupils to ELSA for an increased level of support for them to access the wider curriculum.
Through ELSA we provide a modified curriculum in an environment based on the six principles of nurture.

Our Family Links worker is part of the Pastoral Team at John Hampden Primary School and can offer support to families to ensure children reach their full potential at school and at home.

pageCache.text:
Wellbeing
Wellbeing at John Hampden Primary School
At John Hampden Primary School, we believe that promoting wellbeing in school is essential for fostering a positive and supportive environment where children can thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. Wellbeing encompasses various aspects, including physical health, mental health, emotional resilience, and social connections.
Physical Health: Encouraging regular physical activity and healthy eating habits is crucial. At John Hampden we promote exercise, such as daily mile runs; two hours of dedicated PE sessions per week; Excalibur Challenge (an inter-house sports competition 3 times during the year); an extensive range of clubs and Wake and Shake to name but a few! Providing nutritious meals and snacks also supports children’s physical wellbeing so we encourage healthy lunch boxes and snacking as well as providing the option for hot meals, cooked freshly on the school premises.
Mental Health: Addressing mental health is vital for overall wellbeing. At John Hampden Primary School we place PSHE at the centre of our curriculum and follow the Jigsaw Scheme which encompasses a mindful approach to wellbeing. We are currently a Flagship School for Jigsaw due to our dedication and exemplary teaching and provision for PSHE. The Sanctuary is a lunch time space available to the children, which provides a safe, inclusive, welcoming and calm environment for those seeking peaceful activities and the chance to engage with our ELSA and Family Links Worker if they wish.
Emotional Resilience: Building emotional resilience helps children cope with challenges and setbacks. At John Hampden School we teach skills like problem-solving, self-regulation, and positive thinking through our curriculum and classroom activities. Encouraging a growth mindset and celebrating achievements, no matter how small, can boost children’s confidence and resilience and our weekly Achievement Assemblies link to PSHE celebrations throughout the week. Children are mentioned by name and awarded stickers for their accomplishments. At John Hampden, we have adopted Zones of Regulation throughout the school; we want to teach our children good coping and regulation strategies so they can help themselves when they experience anxiety and stress. By teaching them how to cope with these feelings, they will be better prepared to build resilience for learning and social challenges.
Social Connections: Fostering strong social connections is key to wellbeing. At John Hampden Primary School, we create opportunities for children to build friendships and develop social skills through group activities, collaborative projects and our buddy system, whereby pupils are paired with a younger or older child from the school for reading, playing, encouraging, supporting and mentoring. Our Young Carers group meet termly. This gives children who care for family members the opportunity to engage in fun activities such craft, cooking and film afternoons. Through The Hampden Way, we promote kindness, teamwork, and endeavour throughout the school community, helping to create a supportive and inclusive atmosphere.
By prioritising wellbeing, primary schools can help children develop the skills and habits needed for a healthy, balanced, and fulfilling life. Investing in wellbeing not only enhances academic performance but also contributes to the overall happiness and success of students. For more information please use the following links:

French
Intent
At John Hampden Primary School, we believe that a high-quality languages education should spark curiosity and broaden children’s understanding of the world. In line with the National Curriculum for Modern Foreign Languages, our teaching aims to enable pupils to express their ideas and thoughts in another language and to understand and respond to its speakers, both in speech and writing.
Learning another language empowers children to interpret, create, and share meaning across cultures, while also strengthening their overall literacy skills. In Key Stage 2, we teach French, providing a balanced approach to spoken and written language. As a Romance language descended from Latin, French shares similarities with Spanish, Italian, and Portuguese, offering an excellent foundation for further language learning at Key Stage 3 and beyond.
Implementation
At our school, we implement the French Scheme Language Nut to ensure high-quality language learning experiences for all pupils. Our approach is guided by the following principles:
Impact
Pupil progress in Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) is recorded, monitored, and assessed in line with the National Curriculum. Assessment is based on class observations of listening and speaking activities as well as written evidence in pupils’ books. Informal assessments are an important part of the process, as they allow teachers to take account of pupils’ understanding, their way of thinking, and their language skills development, ensuring that planning is responsive and targeted.
The outcomes of all assessments are used to inform planning and to target individuals and/or groups where necessary, ensuring that every learner is supported effectively.
Parents receive an annual written report that includes their child’s progress in MFL. Through these measures, we ensure that pupils develop confidence, competence, and enthusiasm for language learning, while teachers maintain a clear understanding of progress and next steps

Music
Intent
At John Hampden School, we are committed to inspiring creativity and confidence through a rich and inclusive music curriculum. We believe music should be a joyful and expressive part of every child’s education. Through singing, composing, performing and listening, pupils develop as curious musicians who appreciate a wide range of styles, traditions and cultures.
Children take part in productions, choir events, instrument learning and musical celebrations throughout the year, helping them grow as performers and collaborators. Through XYZ Primary, the carefully sequenced curriculum ensures all pupils understand how music is created and communicated, while also recognising the important role it plays in well-being, community and marking significant moments in life.
We aim to nurture musicians who are confident, reflective and enthusiastic – children who value music both in school and beyond.
Implementation
Our music curriculum follows XYZ Primary and is carefully sequenced to develop pupils’ skills, creativity and confidence from Early Years through to Year 6. Lessons are practical, engaging and built around essential learning objectives: to perform, to transcribe, to compose and to describe music. We are committed to inclusion, and lessons are adapted to ensure that all children—regardless of need, ability or starting point—can participate fully and experience success as musicians.
In Key Stage 1, children learn to use their voices expressively through singing, chants and rhymes. They explore a range of tuned and untuned instruments, learning to play musically and with enjoyment. Pupils begin to understand the inter-related dimensions of music by making and combining sounds, laying strong foundations for future learning.
In Key Stage 2, pupils build on these early experiences by performing both solo and in ensembles, using their voices and instruments with increasing accuracy, control and expression. They improvise and compose music using the inter-related dimensions, applying their knowledge creatively and independently. Children develop their listening and aural memory skills, begin to read and write simple musical notation, and explore high-quality music from a broad range of cultures, traditions and historical periods. They also gain an understanding of how music has developed over time.
Our inclusive and progressive approach ensures that all pupils leave our school as confident performers, thoughtful listeners and imaginative composers who can talk about, enjoy and value music in meaningful ways.
Impact
The impact of our music curriculum is seen in the confidence, creativity and musical understanding our pupils develop as they progress through the school. Close liaison between the class teacher and the specialist music teacher ensures that learning is well-matched to pupils’ needs. The music teacher records progress termly, providing ongoing feedback that supports each child’s development.
Pupils regularly share their compositions and performances with one another, offering constructive comments that help them refine their musical ideas and grow as reflective, supportive musicians. This collaborative approach strengthens confidence and nurtures a sense of pride in their achievements.
We value strong partnerships with families, including liaison with pupils and parents when children take instrumental lessons outside school and regular performance assemblies where parents are invited. At the end of the year, all children receive a music comment on attainment in their school report, enabling parents to see the progress their child has made and the skills they have developed.
Through this comprehensive and connected approach, pupils leave our school with a secure understanding of musical concepts, well-developed performance skills and a lifelong appreciation for music.

Parent Information
At John Hampden School, we are committed to working in close partnership with parents and carers to support children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). As part of this, we offer parent workshops designed to share information, build understanding and provide practical strategies that can be used at home and in school.
The slides from our recent parent workshops, available below, cover a range of topics linked to SEND and inclusion. They are intended to help explain how we support children in school, outline key approaches we use, and offer guidance to support your child’s learning, wellbeing and development. Whether you were able to attend or not, we hope these resources are helpful and reassuring.
We also have a programme of upcoming parent workshops, listed below. These sessions provide an opportunity to:
All parents and carers are very welcome to attend. We strongly believe that by working together and sharing knowledge, we can best support every child to thrive.
If you would like further information about any of the workshops, or if there is a topic you would find helpful in the future, please do not hesitate to contact the school.

Art
Intent
At John Hampden School we take pride in all the artistic talents of our pupils and we recognise the vital contribution Art and Design make to our children’s cognitive, social, emotional and physical development. It is a valued and integral part of our school ethos, and we aim to provide a broad, balanced and inclusive Art curriculum.
Art is an ongoing process through which all children are given opportunities to develop specific skills, knowledge, understanding and an increasing self-confidence to enable them to work in a variety of medium, style and forms. It enables children of all abilities to use their creative imagination to achieve their potential with guidance and given criteria, differentiated where appropriate.
Children work individually and collaboratively with other pupils, adults and members of the community on art projects to develop their social and personal skills. Art is not taught in isolation but is linked wherever appropriate to other areas of the curriculum and community, giving children the opportunities to develop specific art skills and reinforce skills already established, and to see art within the greater environment.
Implementation
The children gain good quality of provision in art and design, which is planned using Access Art – a National Curriculum Scheme designed to broaden and enrich childrens’ experience of art through a balanced and diverse curriculum. Cross-curricular links are used wherever possible to ensure that the arts are not seen in isolation but rather as an intrinsic part of school life.
We recognise the fact that we have children of differing ability in all our classes, and so we provide suitable learning opportunities for all children by matching the challenge of the task to the ability of the child. We believe that the arts provide children with the opportunities to develop their self-esteem, which will, in turn raise their confidence in other areas of the curriculum.
Inclusive is at the heart of our teaching and activities are adapted to suit a range of abilities
Impact
We believe assessment should inspire creativity, not limit it. Throughout each pathway, teachers use observation, questioning, and sketchbook reviews to understand how pupils are developing their ideas. Progress is measured against age-related expectations and shared with parents annually. Lessons are built around clear learning objectives and success criteria, while encouraging pupils to experiment, take creative risks, and respond to feedback.
Through AccessArt, teachers model the behaviours of real artists—exploring, adapting, and reflecting alongside pupils. Adaptation of tasks ensures every child, including those with SEND and higher-attaining learners, is supported and challenged. Self and peer assessment are woven into lessons through sketchbook reflections and verbal feedback, helping pupils grow as confident, independent artists.

Computing
Intent
At John Hampden Primary School, we aim to provide an excellent and enjoyable education within a safe, secure, and caring environment where every individual is valued and respected. We strive to help all pupils reach their full potential and grow into responsible, caring citizens.
We recognise the importance of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) as an essential life skill and an integral part of the National Curriculum. Our intent is to ensure pupils have access to quality resources and a structured, progressive approach to developing the skills needed to use technology effectively for learning, communication, and creativity. As part of this, we are committed to teaching pupils how to use the internet safely and responsibly, understanding their role in a growing global community where digital citizenship is vital.
Implementation
At John Hampden Primary School, Computing is taught both as a discrete subject and through cross-curricular links where appropriate. Pupils access the curriculum using a range of resources, including laptops, PCs, tablets, and programmable devices.
We follow the Purple Mash scheme of work to ensure progression, supplemented in upper Key Stage 2 by our bespoke curriculum map, which develops key skills in everyday applications such as Word, PowerPoint, and Excel. Modules are planned in line with the National Curriculum, enabling clear progression and achievement of objectives.
The Computing subject leader monitors resources and provision, ensuring pupils have access to quality hardware and software. Teachers plan to support all learners effectively, promoting safe and responsible use of technology and the internet within a growing global community.
Our curriculum is designed to ensure that every child—regardless of ability, social or cultural background, disability, English as an Additional Language (EAL), or Special Educational Needs (SEN), whether statemented or not—has full access to learning and the opportunity to thrive alongside their peers.
We place particular emphasis on the flexibility that technology brings, enabling all pupils, especially those with SEN and disabilities, to engage meaningfully with the curriculum. Through adaptive tools and resources, we ensure that every learner can participate, progress, and succeed in a supportive and inclusive environment.
By the end of Key Stage 2, pupils will confidently design, write, and debug programs; use logical reasoning; understand networks and the internet; evaluate digital content; and apply a range of software tools to collect, analyse, and present information securely and responsibly.
Impact
he impact of our Computing curriculum is measured through continuous monitoring and assessment. The Computing Leader oversees standards of teaching and learning, ensuring consistency and progression across all year groups. Teachers maintain online portfolios using Purple Mash, which include work samples from all areas of the curriculum taught, providing a comprehensive record of pupil achievement.
Assessment is ongoing through observations and review of completed work, supported by the Purple Mash assessment tool, which offers detailed exemplification for each key learning intention. This enables staff to accurately identify attainment and inform next steps. In EYFS, pupil progress is tracked using Evidence Me against the Early Learning Goals, ensuring a strong foundation for future learning.
Through this rigorous approach, pupils develop secure knowledge and skills in Computing, becoming confident, safe, and responsible users of technology.

Geography
Intent
At John Hampden School, Geography is the study of people, their behaviour, and the environment in which they live. Through a broad range of engaging and relevant topics, our pupils develop a deep understanding of their place in an ever-changing world. Pupils explore the complexity of human lives, preparing them for future roles and responsibilities while encouraging them to make a positive difference.
By making links to History and PSHE, we enable children to compare past and present contexts and understand how citizens shape local and global environments. We aim to develop knowledge and understanding of places and cultures across the world, teach essential graphic skills and recognise global connections through travel and trade. Pupils explore environmental issues at local, regional, and global levels, celebrate diversity, and understand the multicultural world we live in. Through comparing and contrasting different locations across the globe, children gain a rich perspective on the world and their role within it. Our pupils become informed, thoughtful, and responsible global citizens, ready to navigate and shape the world around them.
Implementation
Geography is taught as a discrete subject in termly units three times a year, with purposeful links to other areas of learning. Our curriculum is designed to give pupils a greater sense of the wider world—developing not only factual knowledge but also a critical approach to learning. Pupils are encouraged to ask and answer challenging questions, describe, explain, and justify their thinking.
Topics are carefully chosen to reflect our school community while contrasting with global contexts, helping pupils identify similarities and differences between themselves and others. In Key Stage 1, children start by exploring their local areas and begin to compare their local environment with contrasting ones. In Key Stage 2, pupils broaden their perspective by studying countries further afield, comparing ways of life and learning to be compassionate and considerate toward diverse cultures.
Fieldwork is an essential part of our approach, providing pupils with hands-on experiences that bring learning to life. Through observing, measuring, and recording in real environments, pupils develop practical skills, deepen their understanding of geographical concepts, and connect classroom learning to the world around them.
Adaptive strategies are used to ensure full access to the curriculum regardless of ability or background to ensure every child has the chance to demonstrate their geographical skills and understanding.
This structured approach ensures pupils leave John Hampden as informed, thoughtful global citizens, ready to navigate and shape the world.
Impact
Pupils leave John Hampden with a secure understanding of the world around them and the ability to think critically about geographical issues. They can ask and answer challenging questions, describe, explain, and justify their ideas, and demonstrate empathy and respect for different cultures and environments.
Progress is monitored by class teachers. Feedback provides next steps and informs future planning, responding to the needs of the class and individuals. The Geography Co-ordinator checks coverage against National Curriculum objectives and reviews pupils’ work through book scrutiny and learning walks. Parents and Carers are kept informed of their child’s progress through annual reports.
As a result, pupils become confident, informed, and responsible global citizens, prepared for the challenges of an ever-changing world.

History
Intent
At John Hampden School, we aim to spark children’s curiosity about the past through an inspiring and challenging curriculum. Pupils explore significant people, events and periods in creative ways that develop their enquiry, analytical and problem-solving skills.
We teach children to make connections across different periods of history, to question the reliability of sources and to understand that historical interpretations can vary. Diversity is woven throughout our curriculum, helping pupils recognise how different perspectives shape our understanding of the past.
In line with the National Curriculum, we ensure pupils gain a secure chronological understanding of British and world history, develop key historical vocabulary and concepts, and learn how to use evidence to debate and form well-reasoned historical arguments and justifications.
Implementation
At John Hampden School, History is taught through an engaging, knowledge and skill-based approach that allows children to explore the past in meaningful and exciting ways. Lessons are carefully sequenced to build pupils’ knowledge, develop their skills of enquiry and support a secure sense of chronology from the earliest years.
Our teaching provides regular opportunities for pupils to ask questions, investigate evidence and carry out research, helping them to develop the skills of historical enquiry. Children explore the roles of significant individuals and key events, both in Britain and across the wider world, gaining an understanding of how these have shaped the society we live in today and how the past continues to influence the present.
We make use of stories, artefacts, photographs, visits and visitors to bring history to life and ensure learning is rooted in real experiences. Local history is an important part of our curriculum, enabling pupils to explore how their own community has changed over time.
Throughout their learning, children also examine diversity within past civilisations, developing an appreciation of how different cultures and groups have contributed to history in varied ways.
Impact
Our history curriculum equips pupils with a secure understanding of the past and an appreciation of how historical events, people and developments have shaped the world they know today. As children move through the school, they build a strong sense of chronology and develop the ability to ask thoughtful questions, analyse evidence and form their own interpretations of historical events.
Pupils leave John Hampden School with a broad knowledge of British and world history, an understanding of diversity across different civilisations and the confidence to discuss how the past continues to influence the present. They demonstrate growing independence in their research skills and show an increasing ability to make connections across different periods of time.
The history co-ordinator checks pupils’ progress against National Curriculum objectives and monitors learning through book scrutinies and learning walks. They ensure that depth of learning develops progressively over time and that teaching enables all children to build on prior knowledge effectively. Findings from monitoring are used to support staff, refine curriculum planning and ensure consistently high-quality provision across the school

Maths
Intent
At John Hampden School, our mathematics curriculum is built on the expectations of the National Curriculum in England: Mathematics Programmes of Study (2020) and the Early Years Foundation Stage Statutory Framework (2014). Our aim is to ensure all children develop strong mathematical foundations that enable them to think logically, reason confidently and apply their learning with accuracy and understanding.
We want our pupils to become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics through regular, varied practice and opportunities to deepen their conceptual understanding. Children are encouraged to reason mathematically – exploring patterns, forming generalisations and using precise mathematical language to justify their thinking.
Pupils apply their knowledge to a range of routine and non-routine problems, learning to break tasks into manageable steps and to persevere when faced with challenge. As maths is an essential part of everyday life, we make meaningful links to real-life contexts and other areas of the curriculum, helping children recognise the value and purpose of what they learn.
Through engaging, practical and enjoyable experiences, we nurture confident mathematicians who develop positive attitudes, secure functional skills and a lifelong curiosity about the mathematical world around them.
Implementation
At John Hampden School, we follow the White Rose programme for medium-term planning. This provides a clear, consistent and progressive structure from Nursery to Year 6, ensuring full coverage of National Curriculum objectives and continuity in calculation methods.
To build strong mathematical understanding, we:
Through this structured and supportive approach, all children are enabled to progress confidently and become capable, enthusiastic mathematicians.
Impact
Our maths curriculum enables pupils to develop secure knowledge, confidence and enjoyment of the subject. By the end of their time at John Hampden School, pupils can reason mathematically, solve problems independently and apply their understanding to real-life situations. Their self-esteem grows as they master key skills and approach challenge with resilience and positivity.
The Maths for Life programme supports pupils with additional needs by developing essential, practical mathematical skills for everyday life. Teachers use formative assessment to track understanding throughout the year, while termly PUMA papers and SATs materials provide standardised information to monitor progress and ensure pupils are on track.
Impact is monitored by the maths coordinator through book looks, lesson observations and assessment reviews, ensuring secure progression and high-quality teaching.
Together, these approaches ensure all pupils develop confidence, resilience and a lasting enthusiasm for mathematics.

PE
Intent
At John Hampden School, Physical Education is a key part of our curriculum because it supports pupils’ physical development, emotional wellbeing, cognitive growth and social skills. Our aim is to offer a broad, balanced and inclusive PE curriculum that enables every child to feel confident, successful and motivated in a variety of physical activities. We promote resilience, teamwork, fair play and leadership, while recognising individual strengths and personal progress. Through a wide range of sports and clubs, we provide positive experiences and structured challenges that help children value physical activity, develop healthy habits and foster a lifelong enjoyment of sport.
Implementation
We deliver a high-quality, progressive and inclusive curriculum, through the REAL PE and Get Set 4 PE schemes, ensuring clear development in agility, balance, coordination, teamwork and healthy competition.
Lessons allow all pupils to achieve and progress, through adaptive practice, tailored challenges, adapted equipment and flexible grouping to support full participation, particularly for pupils with SEND or specific physical needs.
Children build skills specific to a variety of sports such as football, gymnastics, netball, hockey, tag rugby, cricket, rounders and athletics, building a wide base of sport-specific skills, alongside specific units of work which develop fundamental PE skills. Swimming and water safety education are provided for Years 4–6, with additional sessions available to support pupils in meeting National Curriculum expectations.
In the Early Years Foundation Stage, physical development is embedded through daily play, movement exploration and access to indoor and outdoor resources that promote strength, coordination and independence. Across the school, learning is sequenced to build on prior knowledge and increase challenge, ensuring all pupils can thrive.
Impact
By the end of their time at John Hampden School, pupils demonstrate confidence and competence in a wide range of physical skills and sports, showing resilience, teamwork, sportsmanship and leadership.
They experience healthy competition through intra- and inter-school events and understand fairness, respect and determination. Pupils work towards meeting swimming requirements and learn essential water safety skills. The PE coordinator monitors curriculum coverage to ensure relevance and challenge. Most importantly, children leave with positive attitudes towards physical activity, healthy lifestyles and a lasting enjoyment of sport.

PSHE
Intent
At John Hampden School, our intention is to deliver PSHE as a whole-school approach that supports children’s development as individuals and strengthens their capacity to learn. By placing PSHE, including statutory Relationships, Health and Sex Education (SRE), and Values education at the heart of our curriculum, we nurture kindness, empathy, determination and resilience, enabling children to contribute positively to their local, national and global communities. Using the six Jigsaw themes, our teaching is structured to promote emotional and physical well-being, empower pupils with informed choices, and broaden their opportunities for future success. The Jigsaw programme provides clear progression and consistency, supporting Ofsted’s expectations for Personal Development and Behaviour, as well as our Safeguarding and Equality duties. Through this, we help children understand and respect themselves, find their voice and become equipped for life and learning.
Implementation
At the John Hampden School, PSHE is taught for 1–1.5 hours each week, ensuring knowledge and skills are delivered in a developmental and age-appropriate sequence. Learning is continually reinforced through assemblies, collective worship, our praise and reward systems, the Learning Charter, Zones of Regulation and positive relationships across the school. Teachers deliver weekly Jigsaw lessons to their own classes, with Federation Values embedded daily across the curriculum. Each term’s Jigsaw theme is explored through whole-school assemblies and classroom discussions. With a strong emphasis on pupils’ physical and mental well-being, PSHE remains central to long-term planning, equipping children with resilience, kindness and the values needed for later life.
Impact
Our pupils will be confident, kind and happy learners who are ready to do their best and work collaboratively. They will enjoy coming to school, feel safe, and trust peers and adults to support them. Children develop a secure understanding of the six Jigsaw units and apply this learning to everyday life, both in and beyond school. Across the school, we value every child, promote respect for all and celebrate differences, religions and beliefs. Our strong PSHE curriculum fosters positive attitudes, emotional resilience and pride in belonging to John Hampden, where PSHE shapes our ethos and daily practice.

RE
Intent
We use a creative, topic-based curriculum where children explore a variety of locations and compare life between them; where they are taught to question their surroundings; where they also learn to understand other people and cultures. We think it is important that children learn about the rich diversity of human and physical geography across the world and learn to recognise the issue of sustainability within society – both at a local and global level. Religious education is a statutory subject and forms part of the core curriculum for all pupils at John Hampden School. Religious Education (RE) in this country is distinctive in being locally agreed within each Local Authority and closely aligned to the nature of the community itself. RE rightly strives to be relevant to the lives of young people of all faiths and none and draws on the experience of the local faith communities within The Oxfordshire Diocesan Board of Education
Implementation
Statement Discovery RE meets the requirements of our locally agreed syllabus. By following Discovery RE at school we intend that Religious Education will:
Nurture children’s own spiritual development.
Impact
Our pupils will have developed an enthusiasm for RE and will have benefitted from the experiences and opportunities they have been a part of. All children will have had the opportunity to experience learning about different religions within the curriculum and will have developed understanding, awareness, and an empathy towards other children’s beliefs and views, as a result of these experiences. This will help them develop their own attitudes and beliefs as they progress through life.

Science
Intent
At John Hampden School, we nurture children’s natural curiosity about the world around them. Our science curriculum encourages pupils to ask questions, explore ideas and Big Questions, and make meaningful discoveries through practical, engaging activities. We provide a stimulating environment that challenges children while supporting their individual abilities and interests. By building on pupils’ experiences, we help them understand why things happen and how science shapes their lives on a personal, national and global level. Enrichment opportunities such as science weeks, visits from scientists and external trips ensure children see the relevance of science in everyday life.
Implementation
At John Hampden School, we implement our science curriculum through a rich variety of teaching and learning approaches designed to develop children’s knowledge, skills and understanding. Lessons include whole-class teaching, Kagan group work, paired and independent tasks, role play, practical investigations, research opportunities and the use of ICT such as data loggers, visualisers and Now Press Play experiences. Fieldwork and educational visits further support real-world scientific understanding. A growth-mindset ethos underpins all lessons, with open-ended tasks, increasing levels of challenge, Big Questions and Explorify discussions used to deepen thinking. Pupil-led enquiry and peer mentoring, particularly in KS2, help children take ownership of their learning.
To ensure full inclusion, we use adaptive strategies that remove barriers and enable every child to succeed. These include adapted resources, tailored scaffolding, carefully considered grouping, targeted adult support, visual prompts, adjusted recording methods and opportunities for pupils to demonstrate understanding in different ways.
Assessment is ongoing and responsive. Teachers use observation and feedback for formative assessment and TAPS plans to inform summative assessment. Children record what they know at the beginning of a unit and add to this as a unit progresses to demonstrate knowledge acquired.
Impact
The impact of our science curriculum at John Hampden School is seen in pupils’ growing confidence, curiosity and ability to think and work scientifically. Children develop secure knowledge, ask thoughtful questions and apply their skills independently in practical and conceptual tasks. Their enthusiasm for science is evident in discussions, written work and their readiness for the next stage of learning.
The science coordinator plays a central role in evaluating and improving provision across the school. Regular book scrutiny ensures progression, consistency and high-quality outcomes, while planning oversight checks curriculum coverage, sequencing and opportunities for challenge. The coordinator also supports staff through learning walks and in-house training, helping refine practice and maintain high expectations for all learners.
As a result, pupils make strong progress and gain a deep, meaningful understanding of scientific ideas.
